b: Two jobs: The hyperexcitability of neurons from people with fragile X syndrome is due to a loss of FMR1 transcripts, according to a new study. Investigators compared neurons that had loss of both FMR1 mRNA and its protein product, FMRP, with those missing only the protein and found that altered electrophysiological, metabolic and morphologic attributes all depended on the absence of the transcript. They also report that the FMR1 transcript acts as a riboregulator, inhibiting the activity of other mRNA molecules to regulate levels of a glycolytic enzyme.
